meaning: willing to take bold risks, sometimes to the point of seeming reckless or rude
example: With no money and no team, her audacious plan was to beat the biggest firm in town at its own game.

meaning: easily shaped or changed, whether metal or a person's views
example: At twelve his opinions were still malleable, and one good teacher reshaped how he saw science.

meaning: to drain of energy or strength (not to energize)
example: The humid afternoon enervated the hikers, and by four o'clock nobody wanted to climb another step.

meaning: inclined to keep thoughts and feelings to oneself
example: Usually reticent in meetings, Omar surprised everyone by talking for ten minutes straight.

meaning: clear, logical and convincing
example: Her case was so cogent that even the two critics on the panel changed their votes.

meaning: clearly expressed and easy to understand; also, thinking clearly
example: After pages of jargon, the last chapter was refreshingly lucid, and I finally understood the theory.

meaning: to make a problem or bad situation worse
example: Scratching the rash only exacerbated it, turning a small itch into a swollen red patch.

meaning: to cause a feeling or situation to come about
example: The coach's fairness engendered a loyalty that held the team together through three losing seasons.

meaning: to reject firmly and refuse to accept or be linked with
example: Years later the author repudiated her early essays, saying she no longer believed a word of them.

meaning: to make something less severe, harmful or painful
example: Planting trees along the street helped mitigate the summer heat for people walking below.

meaning: harmless and unlikely to offend or upset anyone
example: The question seemed innocuous, but it started an argument that lasted all through dinner.

meaning: quick to become angry
example: The irascible landlord shouted at anyone who knocked on his door before noon.

meaning: to mock or speak about with contempt
example: Critics derided the film as silly, yet audiences lined up around the block to see it.

meaning: too eager to please or obey, in a way that seems insincere
example: The obsequious waiter laughed at every joke the rich guest made, however weak.

meaning: impossible to calm or satisfy, especially in anger or opposition
example: Her rival was implacable; no apology or offer would end the feud.

meaning: joking at the wrong moment; not meant seriously
example: His facetious reply about selling the dog annoyed his worried sister.

meaning: to copy someone you admire, hoping to match or beat them
example: Young players emulated her serve, tossing the ball high and striking it late.

meaning: playfully odd or fanciful; acting on sudden ideas
example: The cafe's whimsical decor included teacups hanging upside down from the ceiling.

meaning: severely plain and without comfort or decoration; also strict
example: The monks lived in austere cells with a bed, a stool and nothing on the walls.

meaning: feeling sorry and guilty for something one has done
example: Contrite after the accident, he paid for the repairs and apologized in person.

meaning: spending money or resources wastefully
example: After a prodigal year of parties and taxis, she had nothing left for rent.

meaning: to grow or spread quickly
example: Small coffee shops burgeoned in the neighborhood once the university opened.

meaning: in original condition; perfectly clean and unspoiled
example: The used car was pristine, with no scratches and the plastic still on the seats.

meaning: lacking flavor, interest or energy
example: The soup was insipid until someone added salt, lime and a handful of herbs.

meaning: to make a bad situation better
example: New bus routes ameliorated the commute for workers in the outer suburbs.

meaning: concerned with beauty or artistic taste
example: The arches were purely an aesthetic choice; the bridge would have stood just as well without them.

meaning: to keep changing one's mind between options
example: He vacillated between the two job offers for weeks, until both companies stopped waiting.

meaning: overly concerned with small rules or with showing off knowledge
example: Her pedantic habit of correcting everyone's grammar made dinner parties tense.

meaning: changing mood or behavior suddenly and without reason
example: The capricious spring weather swung from sunshine to hail within an hour.

meaning: to prove a statement or claim wrong
example: The lab's new data refuted the old claim that the drug had no side effects.

meaning: showing great care about every detail
example: A meticulous editor, she checked every date and every name before the book went to print.

meaning: to express disapproval or disappointment to someone
example: Her mother never shouted; she simply reproached her with a quiet, tired look.

meaning: lasting a very short time
example: The band's fame was ephemeral: one hit song, one summer, and then silence.

meaning: departing from what is normal or expected
example: One aberrant result made the scientists repeat the whole trial from the start.

meaning: a strong, settled dislike
example: Their antipathy went back to school, when one had copied the other's homework.

meaning: drawing from many different sources or styles
example: His eclectic playlist moved from jazz to folk to Korean pop without warning.

meaning: ordinary and dull; part of everyday routine
example: Between the exciting launches, most of the job was mundane paperwork.

meaning: official approval, or an official penalty; it can mean either
example: The council gave its sanction to the street festival, closing three blocks for the day.

meaning: to remove a need or difficulty in advance
example: A clear sign at the entrance obviated the need for a guard to give directions.

meaning: always calm, even under stress
example: The imperturbable pilot announced the engine trouble as if he were reading the weather.

meaning: eager and quick readiness
example: She accepted the invitation with alacrity, replying within a minute.

meaning: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but mildly
example: The librarian admonished the boys for talking, then went back to her desk.

meaning: stubbornly refusing to change one's mind
example: Despite the petition, the obdurate manager refused to reopen the old entrance.

meaning: unable to be changed
example: To a child, the bedtime rule seemed immutable, like a law of nature.

meaning: willing to agree or cooperate
example: The landlord was amenable to a later move-out date if they paid for the extra week.

meaning: to calm someone's anger, often by giving them something
example: To placate the angry passengers, the airline handed out meal vouchers.

meaning: calm and unemotional by temperament
example: Even when the stove caught fire, the phlegmatic chef simply reached for the lid.

meaning: a remark used so often it has lost its force
example: The speech was a string of platitudes about hard work and following your dreams.

meaning: so ordinary that it is boring
example: After a banal first act, the play finally came alive in the second half.

meaning: to give a false impression of, or to show something to be false
example: His calm voice belied the panic he felt as the plane dropped.

meaning: seeming reasonable at first but actually wrong
example: The ad's specious logic suggested that a drink must be healthy because athletes drink it.

meaning: to flatter someone too eagerly to win favor
example: Reporters fawned over the young star, praising even her shortest answers.

meaning: copied or adapted from others; not original
example: Critics called the novel derivative, a tired copy of last year's bestseller.

meaning: lazy; avoiding effort
example: The indolent cat spent the whole day moving from one sunny spot to the next.

meaning: to officially clear someone of blame
example: The video exonerated the driver, showing that the cyclist had run the red light.

meaning: to avoid telling the truth by speaking vaguely
example: Asked where the money went, the treasurer prevaricated, talking about timing issues.

meaning: bitterly sarcastic; also able to burn by chemical action
example: Her caustic review called the restaurant's bread a crime against wheat.

meaning: cowardly in a shameful way
example: The craven captain was the first one into the lifeboat.

meaning: to overwhelm with a huge amount, like a flood
example: After the ad aired, the shop was inundated with orders it couldn't fill.

meaning: practicing strict self-denial, avoiding pleasure and comfort
example: He kept an ascetic routine: cold showers, plain rice and no phone after dark.

meaning: to use vague language to avoid committing oneself
example: When asked whether taxes would rise, the candidate equivocated for five full minutes.

meaning: to make a bad feeling less intense
example: A long call home assuaged her loneliness during the first week at college.

meaning: talking too much, especially about unimportant things
example: The garrulous taxi driver told us his life story before we reached the second traffic light.

meaning: lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern
example: Voter apathy was so high that only one in five residents showed up.

meaning: gloomy and bad-tempered
example: After the loss, the team sat in morose silence on the long bus ride home.

meaning: a long, angry speech aimed at criticizing someone
example: The coach's half-time harangue could be heard from the parking lot.

meaning: to spread information or ideas widely
example: Volunteers disseminated the safety leaflets to every house on the street.

meaning: a person who dislikes and avoids other people
example: The old misanthrope put a sign on his gate that read: No visitors, ever.

meaning: to take the place of something, often by force or strategy
example: Within a decade, streaming had supplanted the video rental store.

meaning: to draw out a response, answer or reaction
example: The comedian's first joke elicited only a single nervous laugh.

meaning: too bold; acting without the right to do so
example: It was presumptuous of him to start planning the wedding after a single date.

meaning: fond of company; sociable
example: Gregarious by nature, she knew half the people at the party within an hour.

meaning: not see-through; also hard to understand
example: The contract's opaque language left both sides unsure what they had agreed to.

meaning: calm and showing little emotion or energy
example: The stolid guard stared straight ahead while tourists made faces at him.

meaning: speaking smoothly but without real thought or sincerity
example: His glib answer about learning from failure didn't satisfy the investors who had lost money.

meaning: dangerously unstable or uncertain
example: The stack of plates sat at a precarious angle on the edge of the counter.

meaning: to soothe someone's anger or worry
example: A free dessert mollified the diner whose order had been forgotten.

meaning: saying very little; habitually quiet
example: Her taciturn grandfather answered most questions with a nod.

meaning: to support or strengthen
example: Strong reviews bolstered the author's confidence before her second book.

meaning: to regard with deep respect
example: The villagers venerated the old healer and asked her advice on everything.

meaning: understood without being said
example: There was a tacit agreement that nobody would mention the broken vase.

meaning: a long, angry speech of criticism
example: He launched into a tirade about parking fines that lasted the whole meal.

meaning: complete honesty and moral uprightness
example: Her probity was beyond question; she once returned a lost wallet with every dollar still inside.

meaning: done quickly and without care, just to get it over with
example: The guard gave our bags a perfunctory glance and waved us through.

meaning: cheerful and full of energy
example: The ebullient host greeted every guest with a hug and a joke.

meaning: a bitter written or spoken attack
example: The newspaper printed his three-page diatribe against the new parking rules.

meaning: to cancel a law, order or agreement
example: After the protests, the school rescinded its ban on phones at lunch.

meaning: heavy and difficult to carry out
example: The new reporting rules were so onerous that small charities hired extra staff just to fill in forms.

meaning: little known and hard to understand
example: Only three people in the room followed his recondite talk on medieval tax law.

meaning: to cause something, usually bad, to happen suddenly
example: The scandal precipitated the minister's resignation within a week.

meaning: an independent person who refuses to follow the group
example: A maverick in the lab, she ignored the usual methods and found the answer first.

meaning: to criticize formally and severely
example: The board censured the director for hiding the losses from shareholders.

meaning: understood by only a small group with special knowledge
example: The forum was full of esoteric debates about rare typefaces.

meaning: likely to cause argument; or fond of arguing
example: Where to build the new stadium was a contentious question that split the city.

meaning: to increase rapidly in number
example: Food trucks proliferated downtown once the city relaxed its permit rules.

meaning: stubbornly refusing to change opinion or course
example: The obstinate mule sat down in the middle of the path and would not move.

meaning: happening at irregular intervals; scattered
example: Apart from sporadic showers in the north, the weekend will be dry.

meaning: to free someone from a mistaken belief
example: The first week of work disabused him of the idea that the job would be easy.

meaning: showy and designed to impress
example: The ostentatious house had gold taps in every bathroom and a fountain in the hall.

meaning: to come together to form one whole
example: Slowly, the scattered protest groups coalesced into a single movement.
